PullRequest.Title: sessions: sign in again when Dev Tunnels rejects the GitHub session
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #349815

**Connect to Remote Agent Host via Dev Tunnel** lists tunnels with an existing GitHub session that has the tunnel scopes. When the Dev Tunnels service rejected that session, the command reported "Failed to list dev tunnels: Sign in to allow access to your tunnels." and gave no way to sign in. The only workaround was to connect to a tunnel from an editor window. There, Remote - Tunnels asks for an account and creates a new session when the service rejects the existing one.

The command now does the same: when the listing fails with `TunnelAuthenticationRequiredError`, it signs in once more through `ITunnelAgentHostService.signIn` and lists again. It skips this when it has just created the session itself, so a rejected new session doesn't prompt twice. Canceling that sign-in closes the picker without an error notification.

The native tunnel service previously picked the first session with the tunnel scopes. After signing in with a different account, it could therefore send the rejected token again. `signIn` now remembers the account it created a session for, and later tunnel requests prefer that account's session.

The reporter's environment doesn't tell us why the service rejected the session. Retrying with a new session is the recovery that Remote - Tunnels uses for any rejected session.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, have a GitHub session with the tunnel scopes (`user:email`, `read:org`) that Dev Tunnels doesn't accept, for example one whose token was revoked on github.com.
2. Run **Connect to Remote Agent Host via Dev Tunnel**.
3. The command asks you to sign in to GitHub, then lists your tunnels instead of failing.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: passed
- `.\scripts\test.bat --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/electron-browser/tunnelAgentHostServiceImpl.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/connectionDiagnosticsService.test.ts`: passed (67 passing). The new "signs in again once" and "uses the signed-in account" cases fail without their fixes.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/connectionDiagnosticsService.test.ts --browser chromium`: passed (23 passing)
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `node build/oxlint.ts` and `node build/hygiene.ts` on the changed files: passed

Not run: an end-to-end sign-in against the Dev Tunnels service.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect via Dev Tunnel with an accepted existing GitHub session, on desktop or browser
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Read hosted-tunnel status, query GitHub sessions, perform one discovery, then populate the picker. Desktop discovery resolves authentication before awaiting shared-process enumeration. Sorting and diagnostics occur after enumeration, as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the current hosted-tunnel status; the native service returns in-memory status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One status request per command invocation, independent of tunnel count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before authentication and picker creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the authentication extension for sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally two scoped queries per command: the command preflight and the tunnel service lookup. The existing native fallback adds one unscoped query only if the scoped service lookup is empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same query count, scopes, and activation behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both queries are awaited; extension activation and initial session loading can affect cold latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a token and provider to the shared-process tunnel enumeration service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per successful desktop discovery, not one per returned tunnel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate agent-host tunnels through the existing Dev Tunnels SDK.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Desktop: one primary SDK list plus M sequential SDK lists for M configured additional-name entries. Returned tunnel IDs are deduplicated, but configured-name requests are not. Browser-native implementation uses one primary SDK list; embedder implementation delegates one discovery call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical SDK operations and ordering on successful authentication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All discovery calls must finish before the picker becomes selectable.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S authentication sessions, N returned tunnels, and M configured additional-name entries. The added native find scans at most S sessions; existing picker sorting remains O(N log N).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The command awaits each stage. Additional-name enumeration is serial within each desktop discovery. Existing independent background discoveries can overlap; this successful path introduces no new discovery or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The command does not cache discovery results. Existing GitHub persisted-session initialization is shared through a promise; warm ordinary session reads use local provider state. Existing transient renewal/restoration can cross network boundaries, with restoration joining by account/scopes and recording failed attempts. SDK imports benefit from module caching. New preferred-account state does not add authentication queries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both implementations and native shared-process enumeration were inspected; the diff preserves all successful-path boundary counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK pagination, network latency, and actual account/tunnel counts are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The added small account-selection scan neither changes boundary cardinality nor introduces a realistic hot collection workload.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recover from a rejected existing GitHub session, including cancellation or a second rejection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: First discovery fails with the typed authentication-required error; the command then awaits one interactive sign-in and one replacement discovery. A cancelled sign-in exits, and a failed replacement discovery exits through the outer catch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request one interactive session from the authentication extension after rejection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one recovery sign-in per command invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The command terminated with an error after the initial rejected discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Explicit user-authentication recovery blocks replacement enumeration until it completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the existing authentication flow and obtain the GitHub identity for the new token.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One createSession invocation; the existing login flow may offer a bounded sequence of supported authentication methods. A successful ordinary OAuth login performs the existing user-info lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No authentication recovery was invoked from this command's failed-listing branch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the newly supported recovery; cancellation prevents retry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize existing provider sessions and save the updated session set to the keychain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider save on successful ordinary OAuth session creation, proportional to S stored sessions; same-account/scope sessions replace the existing entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No provider save on this failed-listing branch; the same persistence mechanism already served explicit sign-in and initial sign-in.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider session creation awaits persistence before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat authentication resolution and shared-process discovery once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two command-owned discoveries in total. A primary-list 401 performs one failed primary SDK operation; a successful retry performs one primary plus M configured-name SDK operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the failed initial discovery occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The replacement discovery must finish before the picker becomes selectable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing added-session listeners may run a separate silent discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One silent discovery per emitted added-session event, not per session or returned tunnel. Its desktop SDK enumeration has the existing one-plus-M call shape.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These same listeners ran for other successful sign-ins, including a command's initial sign-in; the rejected-existing-session branch did not previously sign in.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by the interactive command, but can overlap its replacement discovery.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit command invocation and one authentication recovery, with S provider sessions and M configured-name entries. N discovered tunnels affect existing diagnostics/picker processing, not recovery retry count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial discovery, sign-in, and replacement discovery are strictly sequential. Existing session-added discovery is independent and can overlap the replacement; no per-tunnel authentication or newly unbounded fan-out is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The native preferred-account map ensures subsequent scoped reads choose the account just signed in. Existing session storage and renewal/restoration caching remain authoritative. There is no recursive retry or retry after a second rejection. Diagnostic activity is capped at 100 entries and successful inventory replaces the previous snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the nested catches bound recovery to one sign-in and one retry, and the existing authentication event handler explains the limited possible overlap.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication duration and SDK request pagination depend on the environment. No live end-to-end authentication timing is available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression. Extra operations implement intentional, bounded recovery of a previously unsuccessful workflow; no runaway retries, collection-multiplied authentication, or lost resource ownership was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect via Dev Tunnel without an existing session, including rejection of the newly created session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pre-existing preflight creates a session, then enumeration runs. The added signedIn flag prevents the new recovery branch from prompting again if that immediately created session is rejected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query existing sessions and create an initial session when absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial scoped query and one createSession invocation; discovery then performs its existing token lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical initial query and session creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial sign-in must complete before enumeration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform initial authentication and tunnel enumeration, with the existing keychain save and added-session discovery side effects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command-owned discovery; a fresh-session rejection does not trigger a second sign-in or discovery. Existing session-added listeners may independently discover once per added event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial authentication, persistence, foreground discovery, and session-event side effects occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication and the command-owned listing are awaited; background discovery is not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One initial sign-in and one foreground discovery per command, with the same S-session serialization and one-plus-M desktop SDK enumeration as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Foreground authentication and enumeration remain serial; existing background auth listeners may overlap as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold provider activation and session restoration remain unchanged. The new local boolean records only whether this invocation created a session and retains no service-lifetime objects.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the newly added boolean is set only after initial createSession succeeds and is explicitly checked before recovery.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Initial provider activation and interactive authentication latency are environment-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The fresh-session branch preserves prior expensive work and avoids an otherwise redundant recovery attempt.

Scenarios.Scenario: Subsequent desktop discovery, management sign-in, deletion, connection, and background relay reconnection after choosing an account
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each operation uses the existing token-resolution path before its existing shared-process request. The diff selects a preferred account from already-returned scoped sessions; it does not fetch another session set or introduce another relay attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve authentication through the extension and invoke existing shared-process discovery, deletion, gateway selection, connection, or reconnection operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same per-operation authentication and transport call counts as before. Management already resolves a provider and then lists tunnels; the added selection scan does not add a query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operations ran, choosing sessions[0] rather than preferring the explicitly signed-in account.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Token resolution remains ahead of each operation; the account-ID lookup runs after the existing scoped query.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the selected token for existing tunnel service and relay operations; management's explicit sign-in still invokes the same authentication provider flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged scheduling and boundary count per operation or existing connection attempt; no new per-tunnel loop is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same network paths and retry scheduling, with the previously selected account token.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested operation awaits its existing network path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S sessions returned for a provider and the existing number of requested tunnel operations or relay attempts. New retained state is at most two account-ID strings, one for each allowed provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The map and scan introduce no scheduling or concurrency changes. Existing management refresh parallelism and per-connection relay lifecycle remain unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The preferred-account map is window/service-local and bounded to github and microsoft. It stores neither tokens nor session objects. Each operation still reads current provider sessions; if the remembered account is absent, existing selection and superset fallback behavior continue.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all new writes use the two-provider union, and all new reads inspect the existing getSessions result without adding a boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual session counts and connection frequency vary; no significant workload for this small local scan is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Retention is constant-bounded and the added local scan is not an actionable performance issue. The repaired account choice is principally a functional authentication fix, not a proven performance-regression fix for internal blame reporting.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all five changed files and every diff page against base 45195eb827afc1b566e870e0ba6f24fd6d47098f. Traced foreground authentication and enumeration, keychain serialization, shared-process SDK calls, auth-event background discovery, browser alternatives, later management/connection consumers, and bounded account-state retention. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying historical performance fix was established. Static analysis only; runtime durations and SDK-internal pagination were not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
